title: Mitigate performance variance from heuristic-driven kernel swapping during mixed-length workloads
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: After a scheduled scheduler heuristic tweak rolled out on 2026-03-08, we observed increased 99th and 99.9th percentile token latency for mixed-short/long sequence traffic on the hosted fleet. Root cause analysis indicates non-deterministic kernel swaps by the scheduler's heuristic scoring function caused suboptimal kernel affinity for certain sequence-length distributions, which amplified attention kernel path regressions under specific batching patterns. This ticket coordinates the follow-up remediation: short-term mitigations, medium-term deterministic affinity scoring, and long-term guardrails and monitoring to prevent recurrence.
actions: [Short-term] Roll back scheduler heuristic patch from rollout 2026-03-08 if tail latency > baseline + 15% during canary window — owner: Bethany Ruiz — due: 2026-03-15

[Immediate mitigation] Add a temporary override to pin kernel selection for the affected model family (openai/compat-* variants) to the previous stable kernel fingerprint — owner: Ethan Morales — due: 2026-03-16

[Medium-term] Implement deterministic kernel-affinity scoring: compute a stable affinity score per model/version/sequence-length bucket and persist per-worker affinities to avoid oscillation — owner: Marco Chen — estimate: 5 pts — due: 2026-03-28
[Medium-term] Launch a canary comparing deterministic-affinity vs heuristic across 5% traffic for 72h with token-level metrics capture — owner: Priya Singh — due: 2026-04-04

[Long-term] Prototype ML-based kernel selector that predicts best kernel variant given input-length histogram and hardware telemetry; evaluate cost/latency improvement vs deterministic approach — owner: Research/Applied ML — estimate: 8 pts — target: Q2 2026
[Ops] Add alerting for kernel-swap rate per-worker and percent of requests observing a kernel residency < 2 tokens — owner: SRE oncall — due: 2026-03-18

[QA] Add synthetic workload tests that exercise mixed-length prefix/cache behaviors to the nightly perf suite; include kubernetes pod-level trace capture for failed cases — owner: QA team — due: 2026-03-22
[Observability] Create dashboards: kernel-affinity-heatmap, per-model-kernel-latency, kernel-swap-rate and add to Console runtime-ops starter set — owner: Observability team — due: 2026-03-19
decision_log: 2026-03-10: Decided to prefer deterministic kernel-affinity scoring over immediate ML-driven selector for medium-term because deterministic approach is simpler to reason about, easier to canary, and has lower risk for new regressions (Ethan, Marco, Aisha).

2026-03-11: Rollback threshold set to baseline + 15% 99p token latency measured on per-worker windows of 15 minutes; this threshold chosen to balance sensitivity to regressions while avoiding noisy triggers (SRE + PM).
2026-03-12: Opted to pin only the affected model family for immediate mitigation rather than global pinning to reduce blast radius.
notes: Investigation links: incident writeup https://confluence.redwood-inference.internal/incidents/2026-03-kernel-heuristic-drift, flamegraphs and kernel timelines attached.
Related PRs: runtime change PR #4872 (scheduler heuristic bump), immediate mitigation PR #4891 (pin kernel fingerprint), deterministic-affinity design doc PR #4923.
Relevant dashboards: https://grafana.redwood-inference/internal/d/runtime-kernel-affinity, kernel-swap-rate panel shows spike aligned with 2026-03-08 rollout window.

Observed signals: 99p token latency increased by 22% for model-family X on n1-gpu workers, CPU saturation marginally higher on workers that experienced rapid kernel swaps, KV-cache hit rate dropped ~3% in affected buckets.

Repro instructions: Run mixed-length perf rig using scripts/perf/mixed_prefix_workload.sh with seq-dist config file 'seq_mix_high_var.json' and enable kernel-swap-logging; expected to reproduce within 30-60 minutes on a 4-GPU pool.
